items.name: Menestra de verduras

items.expl: Artichokes grilled on a hot plate until tender and lightly charred. Finished with olive oil, garlic, and coarse salt.
items.name: Alcachofas a la plancha

items.expl: Aubergine slices lightly battered, fried until crisp, and drizzled with cane honey or molasses. A specialty of Andalusia, especially Córdoba.
items.name: Berenjenas con miel

items.expl: Saffron rice cooked in a wide pan with chicken, rabbit, green beans and white beans. Traditionally eaten at lunchtime, often straight from the pan.
items.name: Paella valenciana

items.expl: Rice cooked in a seafood stock with prawns, mussels, clams and squid. Served in the pan with a lemon wedge.
items.name: Paella de marisco

items.expl: Rice colored black with squid ink and cooked with squid or cuttlefish. Usually served with garlic mayonnaise (alioli).
items.name: Arroz negro

items.expl: A paella-style dish made with short thin noodles instead of rice, cooked in fish stock with seafood. Typically served with alioli.
items.name: Fideuà

items.expl: Hearty Madrid stew of chickpeas, vegetables, beef, chorizo, pork and blood sausage. Often served in stages: broth with noodles first, then the chickpeas and meats.
items.name: Cocido madrileño

items.expl: Rich Asturian stew of large white beans with chorizo, morcilla (blood sausage) and pork belly. A heavy, warming dish.
items.name: Fabada asturiana

items.expl: Slow-cooked lentil stew with chorizo, potato, carrot and onion. A classic home-style dish often on the menú del día.
items.name: Lentejas estofadas

items.expl: Roast suckling pig with crackling skin and very tender meat, a specialty of Segovia. Served in portions with roast potatoes or salad.
items.name: Cochinillo asado

items.expl: Slow roast lamb, typical of Castilla. Cooked in a wood-fired oven and seasoned simply with salt, garlic and sometimes herbs.
items.name: Cordero asado

items.expl: Oxtail braised for hours in red wine with onions, carrots and tomato until falling apart. A specialty of Córdoba and Andalusia.
items.name: Rabo de toro

items.expl: Meatballs of pork and beef simmered in a tomato or onion sauce. Often served with fries or rice.
items.name: Albóndigas en salsa

items.expl: Madrid-style tripe stew cooked with chorizo, morcilla and paprika. Rich and slightly spicy.
items.name: Callos a la madrileña

items.expl: Thick, bone-in aged beef steak grilled over charcoal and seasoned with coarse salt. Usually shared between two people.
items.name: Chuletón de buey

items.expl: Juicy cut of Iberian pork from the shoulder, grilled or pan-seared. Often served with potatoes or peppers.
items.name: Secreto ibérico

items.expl: Chicken pieces fried with plenty of garlic, white wine and herbs. Served with the garlicky juices and often fries.
items.name: Pollo al ajillo

items.expl: Hake in a green sauce of parsley, garlic and white wine, usually with clams and peas. A Basque classic.
items.name: Merluza a la vasca

items.expl: Salt cod cooked slowly in olive oil and garlic until the gelatin forms a creamy emulsion. A Basque specialty.
items.name: Bacalao al pil pil

items.expl: Salt cod stewed in a tomato and red pepper sauce, typical of La Rioja. Served hot in a clay dish.
items.name: Bacalao a la riojana

items.expl: Basque fisherman's stew of tuna, potatoes, peppers and tomato. Thick and warming.
items.name: Marmitako

items.expl: Gilthead sea bream baked inside a crust of coarse salt, which keeps the flesh moist. The crust is cracked open at the table.
items.name: Dorada a la sal

items.expl: Assorted small fish and seafood lightly floured and deep-fried, popular in Andalusia. Served with lemon.
items.name: Pescaíto frito

items.expl: Catalan seafood stew with fish, prawns, mussels and squid in a rich tomato, wine and sometimes almond-thickened sauce.
items.name: Zarzuela de pescado y marisco

items.expl: Spaghetti with a minced meat and tomato sauce, a very common everyday dish in Spain and a favorite with children.
items.name: Espaguetis a la boloñesa

items.expl: Fried eggs broken over a bed of fried potatoes and topped with slices of cured ham. Simple and filling.
items.name: Huevos rotos con jamón

items.expl: Rice cooked in a rich fish stock, from the Valencia region, served with alioli. The fish is traditionally served separately or in the pan.
items.name: Arroz a banda

items.expl: Whole fresh sardines grilled on a hot griddle with coarse salt and a squeeze of lemon. A classic at beach bars and seafood restaurants, eaten with your hands.
items.name: Sardinas a la plancha

items.expl: Sardines skewered on a cane stick and grilled over an open wood fire on the beach, typical of Málaga. Simply seasoned with sea salt.
items.name: Espetos de sardinas

items.expl: Thick steak of Atlantic bluefin tuna seared on the griddle, often left pink inside. Typically served with olive oil, salt and sometimes a soy or onion topping.
items.name: Atún rojo a la plancha

items.expl: Basque-style stew of white tuna chunks, potatoes, peppers and tomato. Hearty fisherman's dish served hot in a bowl.
items.name: Marmitako de bonito

items.expl: Salmon fillet pan-seared or griddled, usually served with grilled vegetables, potatoes or salad. Common on the daily set menu.
items.name: Salmón a la plancha

items.expl: Monkfish cooked in a sauce of white wine, garlic, parsley and often clams or prawns. Firm, meaty white fish served with the sauce.
items.name: Rape a la marinera

items.expl: Sea bass opened flat (butterflied) and grilled, served with garlic and olive oil. Often seen in Basque and Cantabrian grill restaurants.
items.name: Lubina a la espalda

items.expl: Whole turbot grilled over charcoal, a Basque specialty from Getaria. Served with olive oil, vinegar and garlic.
items.name: Rodaballo a la parrilla

items.expl: Clams steamed in a sauce of white wine, garlic, parsley and a little flour or paprika. Great for dipping bread in the juices.
items.name: Almejas a la marinera

items.expl: Mussels steamed open, often with white wine, bay leaf and lemon. Served hot in their shells, a common tapa.
items.name: Mejillones al vapor

items.expl: Razor clams grilled on a hot plate until they open, finished with olive oil, garlic, parsley and lemon.
items.name: Navajas a la plancha

items.expl: Whole prawns grilled on a hot griddle with coarse sea salt. You peel them yourself and eat them with your fingers.
items.name: Gambas a la plancha

items.expl: Crusty baguette sandwich filled with fried battered squid rings, a Madrid classic. Often eaten with a squeeze of lemon or mayonnaise.
items.name: Bocadillo de calamares

items.expl: Simple baguette sandwich with slices of cured ham, sometimes with olive oil or tomato. Sold in bars and bakeries everywhere.
items.name: Bocadillo de jamón

items.expl: Baguette filled with Spanish potato omelette. A cheap, filling lunch or snack.
items.name: Bocadillo de tortilla

items.expl: Large flat pie from Galicia with a bread-like crust, filled with tuna, cod or meat in a tomato and onion sauce. Sold by the slice in bakeries.
items.name: Empanada gallega

items.expl: Small half-moon turnovers filled with tuna and tomato or meat, baked or fried. Common as a tapa or snack.
items.name: Empanadillas

items.expl: Long fried-dough sticks dusted with sugar, crisp outside and soft inside. Typically eaten for breakfast or as a snack, often dipped in hot chocolate.
items.name: Churros

items.expl: Thicker, softer and fluffier cousins of churros, fried and cut into pieces. Usually dipped in hot chocolate or coffee.
items.name: Porras

items.expl: A slice of potato omelette served on bread as a bar snack. Common in Basque and northern bars.
items.name: Pincho de tortilla

items.expl: Small bread roll topped with grilled pork loin, often with cheese or green pepper. A typical Andalusian bar snack.
items.name: Montadito de lomo

items.expl: Skewers of pickled vegetables such as gherkins, olives, peppers and onions, sometimes with an anchovy. Salty, tangy bar snack that goes with beer or vermouth.
items.name: Banderillas

items.expl: Basque pintxo skewer of a green olive, pickled guindilla pepper and anchovy. Salty, briny and slightly spicy.
items.name: Gilda

items.expl: Baguette filled with grilled pork belly, sometimes with cheese or peppers. Salty and rich, popular at markets and bars.
items.name: Bocadillo de panceta

items.expl: Crunchy fried or baked cubes of pork belly with crackling skin. A popular bar snack, especially in Castilla.
items.name: Torreznos

items.expl: A chilled custard made with milk, egg yolks, cinnamon and lemon zest, topped with a thin layer of caramelized sugar. Served in a small clay dish.
items.name: Crema catalana

items.expl: A smooth baked egg custard turned out of its mold and covered in liquid caramel. A classic dessert on the set lunch menu (menú del día).
items.name: Flan de huevo

items.expl: A Galician almond cake made with ground almonds, eggs and sugar, with no flour. It is dusted with powdered sugar, often in the shape of the St James cross.
items.name: Tarta de Santiago

items.expl: A creamy vanilla and cinnamon custard made with milk and egg yolks, usually served cold in a bowl or cup with a María cookie on top.
items.name: Natillas

items.expl: Rice pudding slowly cooked in milk with sugar, cinnamon and lemon peel. It is served cold or warm, often with ground cinnamon on top.
items.name: Arroz con leche

items.expl: A creamy baked cheesecake, often in the Basque style with a deeply caramelized top and a soft, almost runny center.
items.name: Tarta de queso

items.expl: Thick milk custard flavored with cinnamon and lemon, cut into squares, coated in flour and egg, then fried. It is served warm and dusted with cinnamon sugar.
items.name: Leche frita

items.expl: Slices of bread soaked in milk or wine and egg, fried and sprinkled with cinnamon sugar or drizzled with honey. Traditional at Easter, similar to French toast.
items.name: Torrijas

items.expl: A nougat bar made from honey, sugar, egg white and toasted almonds. Comes in a hard (Alicante) or soft (Jijona) version, especially popular at Christmas.
items.name: Turrón

items.expl: Crumbly shortbread-style cookies made with flour, lard or butter, sugar and almonds. They are sold wrapped in paper at Christmas.
items.name: Polvorones

items.expl: Ice cream flavored with nougat, with crunchy almond pieces. A common flavor in ice cream parlors (heladerías).
items.name: Helado de turrón

items.expl: A simple dessert of set sheep's or cow's milk curd, similar to a soft cheese pudding, served with honey and sometimes walnuts.
items.name: Cuajada con miel

items.expl: A light, spiral-shaped sweet pastry from Mallorca made with flour, eggs and lard, and dusted with powdered sugar. Eaten at breakfast or as a snack.
items.name: Ensaimada

items.expl: A rectangular flaky pastry filled with chocolate cream or chocolate bars, sold in nearly every bakery for breakfast.
items.name: Napolitana de chocolate

items.expl: A croissant split open and grilled until warm and crisp, usually served in cafés with butter and jam or with ham and cheese.
items.name: Croissant a la plancha

items.expl: Toasted bread topped with grated fresh tomato, olive oil and salt. It is a staple Spanish breakfast, often served with a coffee.
items.name: Tostada con tomate y aceite

items.expl: Soft, fluffy muffin-shaped sponge cakes made with eggs, sugar, flour and olive oil or sunflower oil, with a lemony flavor. Common at breakfast.
items.name: Magdalenas

items.expl: A heart-shaped puff pastry cookie, crisp and flaky, with a coating of dark or white chocolate. Sold by weight or piece in bakeries.
items.name: Palmera de chocolate

items.expl: A ring-shaped pastry or doughnut, either fried or baked and flavored with anise or lemon. Often covered with sugar glaze, popular at festivals and in bakeries.
items.name: Rosquilla

items.expl: A chilled punch of red wine, chopped fruit, sugar or juice and sometimes brandy or soda. Served in a pitcher, especially in summer. Grape varieties: usually a simple red table wine, most often Tempranillo or Garnacha, mixed with fruit, sugar and spirits.
items.name: Sangría

items.expl: A refreshing mix of red wine and lemon soda or sparkling soft drink, served over ice. Lighter and simpler than sangría.
items.name: Tinto de verano

items.expl: A sweet fortified wine flavored with herbs, served over ice with an orange slice and olive. Often drunk as an aperitif before lunch. Grape varieties: a fortified, herb-infused wine usually based on neutral white grapes such as Airén, Macabeo or Palomino.
items.name: Vermut

items.expl: A dry, slightly sour natural cider from Asturias. It is poured from a height into a wide glass to aerate it and drunk right away.
items.name: Sidra asturiana

items.expl: A cold, creamy, sweet drink made from tiger nuts (chufas), water and sugar, typical of Valencia. Often served with fartons, a sweet pastry.
items.name: Horchata de chufa

items.expl: Beer, served in small glasses. A caña is a small draft beer, a tubo is a taller glass, and a jarra is a mug. Ask for a Mahou, Estrella or Cruzcampo for local brands.
items.name: Cerveza

items.expl: A light shandy of beer mixed with lemon soda or lemonade. Popular in warm weather and less strong than regular beer.
items.name: Clara

items.expl: A mix of red wine and cola, served over ice. Originally from the Basque Country, popular at festivals and among young people.
items.name: Kalimotxo

items.expl: Espresso mixed with an equal amount of hot steamed milk, served in a medium cup. The standard morning coffee in Spain.
items.name: Café con leche

items.expl: A short, strong espresso served in a small cup, the default order if you just ask for 'un café'. Drunk at any time of day, especially after meals. Achtung: In English-speaking countries a 'solo' is not a coffee term, and plain 'coffee' there means filter coffee, not espresso.
items.name: Café solo

items.expl: Espresso 'cut' with a small splash of warm milk, served in a small glass or cup. Popular after lunch or in the afternoon. Achtung: In some English-speaking cafés a cortado is similar, but in Spain the milk is usually just steamed, with little or no foam.
items.name: Cortado

items.expl: A small cup with espresso and sweetened condensed milk in roughly equal parts, often layered in a glass. Very sweet and creamy, enjoyed as a treat, especially in Valencia and eastern Spain. Achtung: 'Bombón' elsewhere means a chocolate candy, and there is no chocolate in this coffee.
items.name: Café bombón

items.expl: You get a hot espresso in a cup plus a separate glass of ice, and you pour it over the ice yourself, adding sugar to taste. A very common refreshing summer order. Achtung: It is not a ready-made iced coffee or cold brew like those found in the US or UK.
items.name: Café con hielo

items.expl: Espresso diluted with hot water, giving a larger, lighter coffee in a bigger cup. Less common than café con leche, and ordered by those who want a longer black coffee. Achtung: It is not the same as the long filter-style coffee Americans call 'coffee'; it is still espresso-based.
items.name: Americano

items.expl: Espresso served with a shot of liquor, usually brandy, rum or whisky, often after lunch or in the evening. Sometimes the liquor is flamed with sugar and a lemon peel. Achtung: In Mexico a carajillo is made with Licor 43, and in English-speaking countries this is just called 'spiked coffee'.
items.name: Carajillo

items.expl: Espresso with sweetened condensed milk, usually layered in a glass, with the milk at the bottom. A sweet dessert-like coffee, typical in Valencia and Murcia, where it is also called bombón.
items.name: Café con leche condensada

items.expl: Decaffeinated coffee made from the machine, usually served as a solo or con leche. You can say 'descafeinado de sobre' for instant decaf, which is also common, so say which you want. Often ordered in the evening.
items.name: Café descafeinado de máquina

items.expl: A Valencian order that blends condensed milk with a splash of milk and a short espresso. Creamier and sweeter than a regular cortado. Achtung: 'Leche y leche' sounds like only milk, but it contains espresso.
items.name: Cortado leche y leche

items.expl: A glass of hot milk 'stained' with just a small amount of coffee, so it is mostly milk and very mild. Common with children or people who want little caffeine, and in parts of Andalusia, especially in the morning. Achtung: In English, 'stained' or 'macchiato' suggests the reverse, mostly coffee with a little milk.
items.name: Manchada

items.expl: An Andalusian order: a glass mostly filled with milk and a little coffee, slightly different from a manchada, where the cloud of coffee floats in the milk. Mild and typically drunk at breakfast. Achtung: In English 'nube' has no coffee meaning, since it simply means 'cloud'.
items.name: Nube

items.expl: A golden lager from Madrid with a light malty taste and gentle bitterness, around 5.5% ABV. It is the classic bar beer in Madrid, served ice-cold in a small glass (caña) with tapas.
items.name: Mahou Cinco Estrellas

items.expl: A pale Pilsner-style lager from Barcelona, crisp and lightly bready with mild hops, about 4.6% ABV. It is the typical Catalan beer, often ordered as a caña or a tercio in bars and beach cafés.
items.name: Estrella Damm

items.expl: A golden lager from A Coruña, slightly fuller and more malty than most, about 5.5% ABV. It is hugely popular in Galicia and northern Spain, and is poured as a caña or sold in bottles.
items.name: Estrella Galicia

items.expl: A pale, light lager with a soft malt flavor and mild bitterness, about 4.5% ABV. Found all over Spain, it is usually drunk cold in bars with snacks.
items.name: San Miguel

items.expl: A amber-gold premium lager from Granada, rounded and malty with a touch of caramel, about 6.4% ABV. It comes in a distinctive green bottle and is served with grilled meat and tapas in Andalusia.
items.name: Alhambra Reserva 1925

items.expl: A light golden lager from Seville with a gentle, slightly sweet malt taste, about 4.8% ABV. It is the everyday beer of Andalusia, served very cold in a small caña.
items.name: Cruzcampo

items.expl: A Barcelona lager with a balanced malt flavor and fresh hops, about 5.4% ABV. It is popular in Catalan craft-style bars, served on tap or in bottles.
items.name: Moritz

items.expl: A golden lager from Zaragoza with a full malt body and distinct hop bitterness, about 5.2% ABV. It is the typical beer of Aragón, ordered as a caña or botellín in local bars.
items.name: Ambar Export

items.expl: A non-alcoholic lager, usually under 0.1% ABV, and light and slightly sweet. Very common in Spain, it is ordered as 'una caña sin' or a bottle, even at lunch or when driving.
items.name: Cerveza sin alcohol

items.expl: A dark-amber to brown lager with roasted malt and caramel notes, about 5-6% ABV. Mahou Maestra, Alhambra Negra and Estrella Galicia Negra are typical examples, and are sipped with cured meats or stews.
items.name: Cerveza tostada

items.expl: A red wine from La Rioja, mostly Tempranillo with some Garnacha, Graciano or Mazuelo. It is dry, with cherry, vanilla and spice notes from oak aging, and goes with roast lamb, grilled meat and chorizo.
items.name: Rioja Tinto

items.expl: A powerful red from Castilla y León, made almost entirely of Tempranillo (locally called Tinto Fino), sometimes with a little Cabernet Sauvignon or Merlot. It is dry, full-bodied and dark-fruited, and is served with roast meats and hearty stews.
items.name: Ribera del Duero

items.expl: A white wine from Galicia made from 100% Albariño grapes. It is dry, crisp and aromatic with peach and citrus notes, and goes well with fish and seafood.
items.name: Albariño Rías Baixas

items.expl: A white wine from Rueda, mostly Verdejo, sometimes with some Viura or Sauvignon Blanc. It is dry, fresh and herbal with grapefruit notes, and a popular choice with tapas, salads and fish.
items.name: Verdejo Rueda

items.expl: A Spanish sparkling wine mainly from Catalonia, made with Macabeo, Xarel·lo and Parellada in the traditional method. It is dry to semi-dry (brut, brut nature, seco) and crisp, and is drunk as an aperitif or at celebrations.
items.name: Cava

items.expl: A fortified wine from Jerez, made from Palomino grapes. It is very dry, pale, light and slightly salty-nutty, and is served chilled with ham, olives, almonds and seafood.
items.name: Jerez Fino

items.expl: A very sweet, dark fortified dessert wine from Andalusia, made from sun-dried Pedro Ximénez grapes. It tastes of raisins, figs and molasses, and is served with desserts or poured over vanilla ice cream.
items.name: Pedro Ximénez

items.expl: A concentrated red from Catalonia, mainly Garnacha and Cariñena (Carignan), sometimes with Syrah or Cabernet Sauvignon. It is dry, full-bodied and mineral with dark fruit, and is suited to red meat and strong cheeses.
items.name: Priorat

items.expl: A rosé from Navarra, typically made from Garnacha. It is dry, fruity and fresh with strawberry notes, and is served chilled with paella, salads and tapas.
items.name: Rosado de Navarra

items.expl: A red wine from Bierzo in Castilla y León, made from Mencía grapes. It is dry, fruity and medium-bodied with red berries and a hint of spice, and goes with grilled meat, mushrooms and cured sausage.
items.name: Mencía Bierzo

items.expl: A very dry, lightly sparkling white from the Basque Country, made mostly from Hondarrabi Zuri. It is high in acidity and low in alcohol, poured from a height into a tumbler, and drunk with pintxos and anchovies.
items.name: Txakoli

items.expl: A deep, robust red from Zamora, made from Tinta de Toro, a local Tempranillo variety. It is dry, tannic and full-bodied with ripe black fruit, and is served with roasts, game and aged cheese.
items.name: Vino de Toro
